decision.candidate: CONJECTURE. Statement: For all integers \( n \ge 1 \), the Li coefficients satisfy the strict log-convexity inequality \( \lambda_{n+1}^2 > \lambda_n \lambda_{n+2} \). Evidence: Computationally tested for \( n = 1 \dots 99 \) using the first 20,000 nontrivial zeros (receipt [receipt not issued by the host]), yielding a minimum ratio \( \lambda_{n+1}^2 / (\lambda_n \lambda_{n+2}) \approx 1.0000124 \). Proof/Refutation path: Could be proved by analyzing the analytic properties of the generating function \( L(z) = \sum_{n=1}^\infty \lambda_n z^n/n! \) derived from the Laurent expansion of \( \zeta'/\zeta \) at \( s=1 \), or refuted if a zero with \( \text{Re}(s) \neq 1/2 \) introduces phase dispersion that breaks the required coefficient alignment. Literature connection: Direct strengthening of Li's equivalence (RH \( \iff \lambda_n \ge 0 \forall n \)); log-convexity is a known structural property for many arithmetic sequences but not previously established for Li coefficients. Bears on the problem: If proven, the inequality implies \( \lambda_n > 0 \) for all \( n \) (given \( \lambda_1, \lambda_2 > 0 \)), which would constitute a proof of the Riemann Hypothesis; conversely, any counterexample would imply the existence of zeros off the critical line and disprove RH.
